key_insight: RPG lets embodied agents improve their robot skills without changing model weights by first reconstructing capabilities from offline data, then practicing those skills in simulation, and finally transferring the gains back to real execution. In simple terms: it turns past experience into targeted self-training for better robot performance.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the high human cost of building, tuning, and maintaining reliable robot skills across many manipulation tasks, especially when perception and control must be integrated and rewards are hard to design.
method: Identify manipulation capabilities from an offline dataset to infer what the robot already knows or can learn.
Construct related practice tasks in simulation to target those capabilities in a controlled setting.
Use execution feedback and privileged simulation information during practice to guide improvement, without updating the model weights.
Transfer the practiced behavior back to real-world execution for improved performance.
impact: This matters because it offers a practical path to continual robot improvement without expensive retraining or manual reward engineering. For AI/ML practitioners, RPG suggests a scalable way to reuse logs and simulation to boost embodied agent reliability.

paper_title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
paper_authors: Yen-Jen Wang, Haozhe Jiang, Shuying Deng, Haoru Xue, Weirui Ye
